{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Convex minimization with a fixed non-Euclidean proximal oracle\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{SO\_\allowbreak{}FO\_\allowbreak{}P01\_\allowbreak{}fixed\_\allowbreak{}non\_\allowbreak{}euclidean}



Single-objective optimization



A hidden finite convex objective is accessed only through the exact proximal point associated with a fixed power of an ell-p distance and a fixed positive coefficient.



\textbf{Status.} Fully optimal on the documented comparison domain



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Objective minimization; task family: Single objective



\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Convex



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; operation: Fixed non euclidean prox; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Deterministic; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed



\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} mode: Probability; quantifier: Algorithm before instance



\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget; measure: N prox



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Minimize an unknown finite convex function \AtlasInlineMath{f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R} globally and return a point with small objective gap.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


Fix \AtlasInlineMath{2<p<s<\infty} and \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda,R>0}. The class consists of finite convex functions having at least one attained global minimizer \AtlasInlineMath{x^\star} with \AtlasInlineMath{\|x^\star\|_p\le R}. No uniform Lipschitz, smoothness, or objective-scale bound is imposed.



The localization ball is only a promise about one global minimizer. It does not restrict query centers or final outputs.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


The only Oracle interface is
\AtlasMath{P_f(c)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\{f(x)+\lambda\|x-c\|_p^s\},\qquad c\in\mathbb R^d.}
 One call returns this unique minimizer only, with no accompanying function value or subgradient.



The positive coefficient \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda} and exponents \AtlasInlineMath{p,s} are public and fixed for the entire interaction. The algorithm may choose the center but may not choose another regularization coefficient or power. Public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{d,p,s,\lambda,R,\varepsilon}; the objective is hidden.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


Return any measurable \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d} determined by the transcript. It need not be a queried center or a proximal response.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


The loss is \AtlasInlineMath{f(\widehat x)-f^\star}, where \AtlasInlineMath{f^\star=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^d}f(x)}.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


One exact fixed-coefficient proximal reply costs one call. The total number of calls is bounded on every instance and every realization of the private seed. Exact internal computation, storage, and specification of arbitrary finite query centers are uncharged.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized / 2/3 success}


Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.



Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.




\AtlasMath{\forall f:\ \Pr(f(\widehat x)-f^\star\le\varepsilon)\ge2/3}




The guarantee is per fixed objective, with an independent private seed and a pathwise query cap.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Deterministic / Pointwise error}


The algorithm is deterministic and adaptive. Queries, stopping, and the output may use the complete preceding transcript. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.



Internal exact-real computation and storage are uncharged. The stated budget holds on every admissible instance and every response history.




\AtlasMath{\forall f:\ f(\widehat x)-f^\star\le\varepsilon}




The error bound is deterministic for every admissible objective.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}


\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Ambient dimension \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{p}: Norm exponent \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{2<p<s<\infty}.



\AtlasInlineMath{s}: Fixed regularization power \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{s>p}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda}: Fixed proximal regularization coefficient \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{R}: Radius of a global minimizer in ell-p \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Target objective error \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\kappa}: Normalized target scale \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\kappa>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\kappa=\lambda R^s/\varepsilon}



\AtlasInlineMath{\rho}: Accuracy exponent denominator \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\rho>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\rho=s+s/p-1}



\AtlasInlineMath{C_p}: Explicit sufficient-dimension coefficient \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{C_p>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{C_p=2+12\cdot64^p}
